headers.name: x-vsr-schema-version
headers.doc: Response-header contract revision; currently `3`.

headers.name: x-vsr-response-path
headers.doc: How the response was produced: `upstream`, `cache`, `fast_response`, `looper`, `blocked`, `rate_limited`, `error` or `fallback`.

headers.name: x-vsr-config-version
headers.doc: Version of the configuration snapshot that served the request.

headers.name: x-vsr-config-hash
headers.doc: SHA-256 of the active runtime document, on routing previews and `GET /api/v1/config`.

headers.name: x-vsr-warnings
headers.doc: Warnings about the response, as an RFC 8941 list: `scan_partial` when a request-stage guard rule read only part of a long input, `guard_overloaded` on the retryable error answered instead of a refusal or a forward that rules unread on an overloaded decision runtime decide, the codes of the `response_guard` rules that annotated the answer, then each `protocol` translation loss with its `action`, `reason` and `field`.

headers.name: x-vsr-selected-recipe
headers.doc: Recipe the effective entrypoint selected; omitted for concrete backend models.

headers.name: x-vsr-selected-decision
headers.doc: Decision the decision engine selected; omitted when no decision matched.

headers.name: x-vsr-selected-model
headers.doc: Model alias the Router selected.

headers.name: x-vsr-replay-id
headers.doc: Router Replay record id, when the record was persisted.

headers.name: x-vsr-cost
headers.doc: Usage priced with the served model's configured pricing; buffered responses only.

headers.name: x-vsr-cost-currency
headers.doc: Currency of `x-vsr-cost`, from `pricing.currency`.

headers.name: x-ratelimit-limit
headers.doc: Limit of the rate-limit window that rejected the request.

headers.name: x-ratelimit-remaining
headers.doc: Requests left in that window.

headers.name: x-ratelimit-reset
headers.doc: Unix time the window resets at.

headers.name: x-request-id
headers.doc: Request correlation id, forwarded to providers; the native gateway adds one when absent, and the management API echoes it.

headers.name: x-content-type-options
headers.doc: `nosniff` on Router Replay management responses.

headers.name: x-envoy-upstream-service-time
headers.doc: Envoy's upstream time on responses in Envoy mode; gateway-parity checks ignore its value.

headers.name: x-envoy-overloaded
headers.doc: `true` on the 503 a full circuit breaker returns, as Envoy sets it.

headers.name: x-vsr-trace
headers.doc: Routing details as an RFC 8941 dictionary of at most 4 KB, for a caller `global.router.headers.debug` allows.

headers.name: x-vsr-session-id
headers.doc: Session id the client pins; without it the Router reads the headers `global.router.headers.session_id_headers` names, in order.

headers.name: x-session-id
headers.doc: Client session id `session_id_headers` accepts by default; providers receive it.

headers.name: x-claude-code-session-id
headers.doc: Conversation id Claude Code sends, which `session_id_headers` accepts by default after `x-session-id`; providers receive it.

headers.name: x-conversation-id
headers.doc: Client conversation id; Router Learning `scope: conversation` protects it, and providers receive it.

headers.name: x-vsr-memory
headers.doc: `off` keeps Router-managed memory out of the request.

headers.name: x-vsr-skip-processing
headers.doc: `true` opts the request out of Router processing when `global.router.skip_processing.enabled` is set.

headers.name: x-vsr-debug
headers.doc: `true` asks for `x-vsr-trace` on the response; honored only for a caller `global.router.headers.debug` allows.

headers.name: x-vsr-cache-control
headers.doc: Response-cache directives for the request, when the plugin's `request_controls` allow them.

headers.name: x-vsr-compression-control
headers.doc: Context-compression directives for the request, when the plugin's `request_controls` allow them.

headers.name: x-vsr-protection-release
headers.doc: Any non-empty value asks router-learning protection for a fresh decision on the request's protection key; `global.router.learning.protection.release.header` can rename it.

headers.name: x-vsr-bench-expected-config-hash
headers.doc: Configuration hash an evaluation request requires; another active configuration fails it with 412.

headers.name: x-vsr-bench-max-inference-calls
headers.doc: Provider-call limit of an evaluation request; only `1` is supported.

headers.name: x-vsr-route-model
headers.doc: Route key: the model whose route the gateway sends the provider request on; the Router drops a client's value and sets its own.

headers.name: x-vsr-upstream-host
headers.doc: Endpoint Envoy reports on the provider response for KV registry writes; removed before the client.

headers.name: x-vsr-kv-source-pod
headers.doc: Address of the pod that holds the source model's KV cache.

headers.name: x-vsr-kv-cache-id
headers.doc: Opaque id of the source KV block.

headers.name: x-vsr-kv-mapper-id
headers.doc: Mapper artifact for the source and target model pair.

headers.name: x-vsr-systemone-backend
headers.doc: Marks a System One request one Router forwards to another, which refuses to forward it again.

headers.name: x-vsr-outcome-source
headers.doc: Outcome provenance a trusted control plane attests to the management API.

headers.name: x-forwarded-for
headers.doc: Client address chain; the native gateway's access log records it, and providers receive it.

headers.name: x-forwarded-proto
headers.doc: Scheme of the client connection; the native gateway sets it when absent, as Envoy does.

headers.name: x-envoy-upstream-rq-timeout-ms
headers.doc: Route timeout the Router sets from the decision's `reliability` block.

headers.name: x-envoy-upstream-rq-per-try-timeout-ms
headers.doc: Per-try timeout the Router sets from the decision's `reliability` block.

headers.name: x-envoy-max-retries
headers.doc: Retry count the Router sets from the decision's `reliability` block, and `0` on evaluation requests.

headers.name: x-envoy-retry-on
headers.doc: Retry conditions the Router sets from the decision's `reliability` block.

headers.name: x-envoy-retriable-status-codes
headers.doc: Retriable status codes the Router sets from the decision's `reliability` block.

headers.name: x-envoy-hedge-on-per-try-timeout
headers.doc: `false` on evaluation requests, so a per-try timeout never hedges.

headers.name: x-envoy-internal
headers.doc: Envoy's internal-request marker; the edge drops it from client requests.

headers.name: x-envoy-retriable-header-names
headers.doc: Envoy retry control; the edge drops it from client requests.

headers.name: x-envoy-retry-grpc-on
headers.doc: Envoy retry control; the edge drops it from client requests.

headers.name: x-envoy-upstream-alt-stat-name
headers.doc: Envoy stats control; the edge drops it from client requests.

headers.name: x-envoy-upstream-rq-timeout-alt-response
headers.doc: Envoy timeout control; the edge drops it from client requests.

headers.name: x-envoy-expected-rq-timeout-ms
headers.doc: Envoy timeout control; the edge drops it from client requests.

headers.name: x-envoy-force-trace
headers.doc: Envoy tracing control; the edge drops it from client requests.

headers.name: x-envoy-ip-tags
headers.doc: Envoy IP tagging control; the edge drops it from client requests.

headers.name: x-envoy-original-url
headers.doc: Envoy redirect control; the edge drops it from client requests.

headers.name: x-envoy-ratelimited
headers.doc: Marks a provider response an Envoy rate limit rejected; the native upstream can retry it.

headers.name: x-authz-user-id
headers.doc: Authenticated user id; `identity.user_id_header` names another header.

headers.name: x-authz-user-groups
headers.doc: Authenticated user's groups, comma-separated; `identity.user_groups_header` names another header.

headers.name: x-authz-team-id
headers.doc: Authenticated team id; partitions the response cache.

headers.name: x-authz-tenant-id
headers.doc: Authenticated tenant id; partitions the response cache.

headers.name: x-vsr-outcome-principal
headers.doc: Opaque attested identity that isolates outcome-ingest rate limits; never persisted.

headers.name: x-user-openai-key
headers.doc: Per-user OpenAI key the authenticator injects.

headers.name: x-user-anthropic-key
headers.doc: Per-user Anthropic key the authenticator injects.

headers.name: x-user-azure-openai-key
headers.doc: Per-user Azure OpenAI key the authenticator injects.

headers.name: x-user-bedrock-key
headers.doc: Per-user AWS Bedrock token the authenticator injects.

headers.name: x-user-gemini-key
headers.doc: Per-user Google Gemini key the authenticator injects.

headers.name: x-user-vertex-ai-key
headers.doc: Per-user Vertex AI token the authenticator injects.

headers.name: x-user-minimax-key
headers.doc: Per-user MiniMax key the authenticator injects.

headers.name: x-user-cloudflare-workers-ai-key
headers.doc: Per-user Cloudflare Workers AI token the authenticator injects.

headers.name: x-vsr-delegated-credential
headers.doc: The requesting user's credential the authenticator attaches; only an upstream with `auth.credential: delegated` receives its value, under its own auth header, and `delegated_credential.header` names another header.

headers.name: x-vsr-internal-auth
headers.doc: In-process request authentication; the Router drops it from every client request.

headers.name: authorization
headers.doc: Bearer credential: a client's key for the Router, and the provider credential the Router sets.

headers.name: api-key
headers.doc: Azure OpenAI key: a client's authenticates to the Router and is removed, and the Router sets the provider's.

headers.name: x-api-key
headers.doc: Provider credential of Anthropic-style APIs.

headers.name: x-goog-api-key
headers.doc: Provider credential of Google APIs.

headers.name: api-subscription-key
headers.doc: Provider credential a catalog provider names.

headers.name: ocp-apim-subscription-key
headers.doc: Azure API Management credential, which a model connection sets through `auth`.

trace_members.doc: SHA-256 of the runtime document that served a config-bound evaluation request.
Provider calls a config-bound evaluation request made.
Per-model usage receipt of a config-bound evaluation request, as JSON.
Model-derived score of the selected decision, such as `0.91`.
Selector or executor that chose the model after the decision matched, such as `static`.
Time spent choosing the model, in milliseconds.
Attempts cross-model fallback made, the primary included, when a fallback candidate served the response.
Decisions whose unknown result `rules.on_unknown` resolved, each with its `policy`.
Client wire protocol, such as `anthropic`.
Provider wire protocol, such as `openai`.
Rendered input tokens of the final automatic-output dispatch, chat template included.
Output token limit of the final automatic-output dispatch, reasoning included.
Matched signal rules as `type:name`, and `type:rule:option` for a choice rule without labels; projections are `projection:name`.
Guard rules that read their input in windows, as `type:name` with `coverage` (`full`, `partial` or `none`) and, for `partial`, the `read` and `windows` counts.
Token count the `context` signal measured.
Domain category the classifier chose, such as `math`.
Reasoning mode chosen for the request: `on` or `off`.
Output kinds of the selected decision's output contract, such as `(image)` or `(text image)`; omitted for a decision that declares none.
Present when a `system_prompt` plugin injected text into the request.
Similarity score of the response-cache lookup.
The matched decision's retention directive: the `drop`, `ttl_turns`, `keep_current_model` and `prefer_prefix` it sets.
Outcome of the `prompt_cache` plugin, with its `reason` and the `inserted` and `preserved` marker counts.
Outcome of the `tools` plugin's selection, with its `candidates`, `kept` and `latency_ms`.
Outcome of the selected decision's `response_guard`, such as `blocked`, with `buffered` when the Router held a streamed answer until the guard read it.
Protection phase: `user_turn`, `tool_loop` or `provider_state`.
Router Learning methods, each with its `action`, `scope` and `reason`.
Models the Looper called, with its `algorithm`, final `model`, `iterations`, `latency_ms` and token counts.
The matched decision the selected one beat, with the `reason` that settled it.
Present when members were left out to keep the trace within 4 KB.

warning_codes.doc: A request-stage guard rule (`jailbreak`, `safety` or `pii`) read only some of a long input's windows, or none, and the request was routed on what it read.
A `response_guard` rule over a `hallucination` signal flagged the answer.
The answer was factual, but a `hallucination` rule had no context to check it against.
A `response_guard` rule over a response-stage `jailbreak` signal flagged the answer.
A `response_guard` rule over any other signal flagged the answer.
Protocol translation changed or dropped part of the request, with its `action`, `reason` and `field`.
Protocol warnings left out to keep the header within 4 KB, with their `count`.
